subject: Nodal readiness affirmation — Hyperion late-stage capacity check
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Kiran Rao <kiran@hyperion.ai>
Cc: Hyperion Sales <sales@hyperion.ai>
Date: 2027-05-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Nodal readiness affirmation — Hyperion late-stage capacity check

Team — looping you all in on a tight ask from Hyperion. They’re in late-stage procurement for a Dedicated deployment and have asked for a firm capacity affirmation ahead of legal/PO so they can commit to a ramped go-live starting 2027-07-01. High-level ask is below; please treat as time-sensitive.

Summary of customer request:
- Account: Hyperion AI (DEAL-8742).
- Peak inference profile: ~35 sustained QPS (p50 request), median request length ~450 tokens, spiky bursts up to +3x for short windows.
- Target model family: 70B dense-ish variant (they may accept an int8 quantized build).
- Desired dedicated pool footprint: initial steady state 12 H100-class GPUs with an additional 6 standby GPUs for burst/failover (customer expects the standby to be warm).
- Optional optimization: with int8 quantization and model sharding, internal estimate says baseline could drop to ~10 GPUs; they are fine with a staged reduction if we can guarantee latency SLO.

What I need from Ops/Capacity (Jonas, Marissa):
1) Confirm node-level availability across US regions for 2027-07-01 -> 2027-10-01 window (can we hold soft capacity for the deal?).
2) If soft hold possible, provide recommended hold counts and the minimal pad (safety buffer) you’d want to reserve.
3) Any nitty-gritty on node types we should promise (H100 vs A100 Q instances) and implications for billing/pricing.

Attachments: provisional-node-map.xlsx (quick nodal mapping & tentative rack placements). I’ve cc’d Hyperion so they see we’re moving quickly.

Next steps: Jonas, can you run a quick inventory sweep and advise on a recommended soft-hold configuration (numbers + regions) by EOD tomorrow? I’ll coordinate the customer ask and align legal on tentative terms after we get confirmation.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: provisional-node-map.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Kiran Rao <kiran@hyperion.ai>, Hyperion Sales <sales@hyperion.ai>
Date: 2027-05-05T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nodal readiness affirmation — Hyperion late-stage capacity check

Ben / Marissa —

Thanks for the context and the node map. Quick inventory note from my side after a first pass against the reservation scheduler and upcoming decomm windows:
- US-west (primary candidate): enough H100-equivalent slots to cover 14 steady GPUs starting July 1, but several are marked to rotate for infra testing the week of 2027-07-04 — I can mark those as \"soft-hold\" but we’ll need a 72hr notice to pull them out of test.
- US-east: limited immediate availability; can supply 4 GPUs as a warm standby pool.
- Recommended soft-hold configuration (balancing customer ask vs pressure on fleet): 12 primary GPUs (US-west), 6 standby split (4 east + 2 west hot-warm). This gives a 33% safety buffer versus the 12 baseline and keeps us under current contention for other Q3 ramps.

Notes on types and options:
- If Hyperion accepts int8 quantization, we can move to A100 or compressed H100 slices and reduce primary to 10 GPUs. That would cut cost and make the hold easier to satisfy. We should capture that as an explicit option in the mutual action plan.
- Billing note: if we promise H100-class capacity we should flag to Finance that pricing for dedicated H100s during Q3 has a transient surcharge due to spot pressure — recommend a provisional surcharge line in the quote.

I'll open CAP-4231 in Jira to track the hold and include the exact node IDs; will attach the node map and a TTL-based soft-hold policy (48h backout for soft-hold, 7d for firm).

Action items:
- Jonas: open CAP-4231 (will do now) + attach node list + proposed SLA impact.
- Ben: confirm if you want the 12+6 soft-hold or prefer to push for a 10-primary (quantized) option to the customer.

Jonas
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: provisional-node-map.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Kiran Rao <kiran@hyperion.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Hyperion Sales <sales@hyperion.ai>
Date: 2027-05-05T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nodal readiness affirmation — Hyperion late-stage capacity check

Ben / Jonas / Marissa —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. A few clarifications from Hyperion’s side before we lock on numbers:
- We prefer the 12-primary + 6-standby plan as the default for procurement; that aligns with our internal runbooks and gives us the headroom for marketing-driven spikes.
- Quantization: we’re open to an int8 pilot for month two of the deployment; we don’t want quantization to be a gating condition for our go-live.
- SLA: we need a documented latency SLO (p95) and a 99.9% availability commitment for the dedicated pool during production hours.
- Procurement timing: legal expects a provisional capacity affirmation to attach to the MSA by 2027-05-10; we understand you may label it a "soft hold" but we need a statement of intent.

If you can provide the soft-hold config + quick note on pricing delta for H100-class promise vs A100 fallback, we can move the PO flow forward today.

Kiran Rao
Director of Infrastructure, Hyperion AI
[Attachment: hyperion-provisional-sla-request.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Kiran Rao <kiran@hyperion.ai>, Hyperion Sales <sales@hyperion.ai>
Date: 2027-05-06T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nodal readiness affirmation — Hyperion late-stage capacity check

Perfect — thanks Kiran, that aligns with what we discussed internally. Jonas / Marissa: please consider this the customer confirmation for a soft-hold of 12 primary + 6 standby (per Jonas’ recommended split), with target ramp 2027-07-01 and a firm go/no-go check 2027-06-15.

Jonas — please launch CAP-4231 and set soft-hold TTL to 2027-06-22 (7 days buffer before the go/no-go), include the node IDs and the pricing delta note for H100 vs A100 in the ticket. Marissa — can you loop Finance/RevOps on the surcharge language so Sales can model the provisional quote? I’ll update the HubSpot deal and flag the legal team to expect the soft-hold note by EOD tomorrow.

Action checklist (internal):
- [x] Customer confirms 12+6 soft-hold (Ben -> Kiran).
- [ ] Jonas: CAP-4231 live + node list + TTL policy + pricing delta (due 2027-05-06 18:00 PDT).
- [ ] Marissa: Attach provisional surcharge language and notify RevOps (due 2027-05-07).
- [ ] Ben: Update HubSpot and notify Legal (done).

I’m marking this thread as high priority — ping me if we hit any blockers.

Thanks —
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-8742]
